title: Reliability and Validity Targets Poster
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Open Educational Resources
description: Explore four archery targets that show reliable and valid, reliable but not valid, valid but not reliable, and neither, then classify six rubric scenarios.

learningObjectives: The learner will classify each of six rubric scenarios as reliable and valid, reliable but not valid, valid on average but not reliable, or neither, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: The terms rubric reliability and rubric validity

dependencies: None. The drawing is inline SVG and the script is plain JavaScript.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then quiz on the same picture
keyQuestions: Are they centered on what matters?
commonMisconceptions: A rubric that gives consistent scores is valid
A rubric with scattered scores is useless
Reliability and validity are the same thing
assessmentOpportunities: Two reviewers always agree, but the scores do not predict learning. Which target?
Scores vary widely, but their average tracks student performance. Which target?
Is a rubric with scattered scores useless?
Can agreement alone prove a rubric is right?

controls.name: Explore and Quiz me buttons
controls.description: switch modes. Quiz me starts a new run.

controls.name: The four targets
controls.description: hover, focus with the Tab key, or click. In quiz mode a click is your answer.
